thread:
sara: heads-up — ran into a frustrating auth error UX in the JS SDK during onboarding. token expired -> SDK throws a generic Error('request failed') with no structured fields. makes retry logic messy and confuses sample apps.

miguel: ouch. can you paste the exact trace?

sara: sure — minimal: `Error: request failed` from src/index.js:45, response body was `Unauthorized` but SDK doesn't attach status/code. we ended up doing string-match on message.

cheng: that's rough. Python behaves slightly better (raises HTTPError with status 401) but still no stable machine-readable `code` like `TOKEN_EXPIRED`. also rate limit 429 in Python lacks `retry_after` on the exception.

alex: TL;DR: SDKs should expose typed exceptions + consistent fields: `error.type`, `error.code`, `status`, `message`, `retriable`, and optional `metadata` map. then app code can do `if (e.code === 'TOKEN_EXPIRED')` instead of hacking strings.

miguel: agree. propose mapping: 401 -> AuthError (code TOKEN_EXPIRED | INVALID_TOKEN), 403 -> PermissionError, 429 -> RateLimitError (include `retry_after`), 4xx-validation -> ValidationError (include `field_errors`), 5xx -> ServerError (retriable=true).

sara: +1. also streaming errors are weird — the stream just ends with a vague message in JS. need a StreamError that carries the last chunk + underlying status if any.

cheng: small nuance: some workflows do token refresh automatically. recommend `AuthError.retriable = true` only when an SDK knows a refresh path and auto-refresh failed; otherwise false. otherwise callers will blindly retry and spike traffic.

alex: implementation notes for SDKs: expose a base class `RedwoodError` with stable properties: `name`, `code`, `status`, `message`, `retriable`, `metadata`. language SDKs map class inheritance to that shape (e.g., `class AuthError extends RedwoodError`). CLI/HTTP clients should return JSON error body like:
```
{
  "error": {
    "type": "AuthError",
    "code": "TOKEN_EXPIRED",
    "status": 401,
    "message": "Token expired",
    "retriable": false,
    "metadata": {"expiry": "2026-03-21T10:00:00Z"}
  }
}
```
so SDKs can parse it into typed exceptions.

miguel: +1 to that shape. can we keep `code` names stable (UPPER_SNAKE) and documented? otherwise people depend on them and we break apps.

sara: we should update quickstart / sample apps to show catch examples. e.g., JS: `try { await client.generate() } catch (e) { if (e.code === 'TOKEN_EXPIRED') { /* refresh token */ } }` and Python: `except AuthError as e: if e.code == 'TOKEN_EXPIRED': ...`.

cheng: question: what about retries for 429 vs 5xx? recommend SDK default retry policy: retry on 429 and 5xx only, respect `retry_after` when provided, and do not retry on 401/403 unless refresh attempted. this aligns with infra expectations.

alex: action items: @miguel — write up a short error spec doc (one-pager) with canonical codes and mapping. @cheng — PR to python-sdk to add typed exceptions + mapping. @alex — JS SDK change to preserve response body on error and throw typed classes. @sara — update onboarding quickstart to include token-refresh example and note error codes.

miguel: I'll draft the spec and ping API for backwards-compatibility concerns. timeline: aiming for spec EOD Fri. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

devex-bot: reminder set — `error-handling-spec` doc assigned to miguel due 3 days.

alex: also we should add automated tests in CI that intentionally return every error shape so SDKs don't regress.

sara: perfect. small UX ask — make default exception `message` human-friendly but also include `raw` for debugging. lots of users rely on the message when debugging from logs.

cheng: noted. I'll include `raw` in the metadata for now.

miguel: thanks all — spec will include examples for streaming, batch, and embedding endpoints. I'll drop link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
